items.title: fix(oauth-provider): leave request bodies alone when the page query is unsigned

labels.name: identity
labels.description: OAuth/OIDC provider, device flow

items.body: Closes #12072 The `oauth-provider-signin` hook re-serialized every POST body whenever the page had any query string. With no `sig`/`ba_param`, `buildSignedOAuthQuery` returns undefined, but the body had already gone through `safeJSONParse` and `JSON.stringify`, so ISO date strings came back as `Date` output and form bodies were sent as JSON under a form content type. Now the hook returns early when there is no signed query. On a signed page, form bodies stay form encoded with `oauth_query` appended, and JSON bodies are parsed with plain `JSON.parse` so date strings are not rewritten. Tests cover unsigned pages (JSON and form bodies sent byte-identical) and signed pages (form encoding kept, dates unchanged, `oauth_query` added). --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #12072 by stopping `oauthProviderClient` from rewriting request bodies when the page query isn't a signed OAuth query. Previously, any query string caused the hook to parse and re-serialize the body even when `buildSignedOAuthQuery` returned undefined, converting ISO date strings to `Date` output and sending form bodies as JSON under a form content type. The hook now returns early when there is no signed query. On signed pages, bodies also keep their original encoding: form bodies stay form-encoded and date strings are left as written while `oauth_query` is added, and JSON parse failures are logged. Tests cover byte-identical JSON and form bodies on unsigned pages and `oauth_query` still being added on signed pages. Written for commit 707b2eda905d195f66f7c61b535f465b9c214ded. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: Client equality gate never suppresses session updates because isJsonEqual returns false for dates
items.body:
### Is this suited for github?

- [x] Yes, this is suited for github

### Reproduction

The client equality gate never suppresses a session update, so every session refetch re-renders `useSession` consumers.

`isJsonEqual` in `packages/better-auth/src/client/equality.ts` handles primitives, arrays and plain objects, but has no branch for `Date`:

```ts
export function isJsonEqual(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean {
	if (a === b) return true;
	if (Array.isArray(a) && Array.isArray(b)) { /* ... */ }
	if (isPlainObject(a) && isPlainObject(b)) { /* ... */ }
	return false; // any Date lands here
}
```

A `Date` is not an array, and `isPlainObject` rejects it because its prototype is `Date.prototype`, so two equal dates fall through to `false`.

That matters because the client parser revives ISO strings into `Date` instances (`parseDates` defaults to `true` in `client/parser.ts`), so the session payload always holds dates.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Sign in and fetch the session twice without changing anything:
   ```ts
   const a = await client.getSession({ fetchOptions: { headers } });
   const b = await client.getSession({ fetchOptions: { headers } });

   a.data.session.expiresAt instanceof Date; // true
   isJsonEqual(a.data, b.data);              // false
   ```
2. `isSessionAtomEqual` calls `isJsonEqual(a.data, b.data)`, so it returns `false`.
3. `withEquality(session, isSessionAtomEqual)` therefore never calls `abort()`, and the `set()` goes through.

Observed on a real instance: `expiresAt instanceof Date` is `true` and `isJsonEqual` on two identical fetches returns `false`.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current behavior**

Two identical session responses compare as different. The equality gate added in #8760 never aborts a `set()`, so every session refetch notifies subscribers and re-renders every `useSession` consumer, even when nothing changed. This is the exact re-render suppression the gate exists to provide.

There is no `Date` coverage in `equality.test.ts`, so this was not a deliberate exclusion.

**Expected behavior**

Two session payloads holding the same instants should compare equal, so the gate aborts the redundant `set()` and no re-render happens.

### What version of Better Auth are you using?

1.6.29

### System info

```bash
Better Auth: better-auth 1.6.29
Affected: packages/better-auth/src/client/equality.ts
Consumers: client/session-atom.ts (isSessionAtomEqual), client/query.ts
Runtime: any (framework agnostic client)
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Client

### Auth config (if applicable)

```typescript
import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/react";

export const authClient = createAuthClient();
// any useSession() consumer re-renders on every refetch
```

### Additional context

`isJsonEqual` is named for JSON values, but the values it actually receives on the client have already been through the date-reviving parser, so dates are always present in practice. Comparing dates by instant keeps the function consistent with the data its only two callers pass it.

items.title: feat(oauth-popup): accept additionalParams like signIn.social
items.body: ## Summary Closes #12119 `signIn.social` accepts `additionalParams`, but `signIn.popup` had no equivalent, so request-dependent parameters such as `ui_locales` could not be passed to the provider. This adds the option to `signIn.popup`, with the same validation as `/sign-in/social`. ## Changes - `signIn.popup` accepts `additionalParams?: Record` and sends it to `/oauth-popup/start` as a JSON query param (same transport as `additionalData`). - `/oauth-popup/start` validates it with `additionalAuthorizationParamsSchema` (string values only; reserved keys such as `state`, `redirect_uri` and PKCE params are rejected) and passes the result to `createAuthorizationURL`. - Invalid params are relayed to the opener as an `invalid_additional_params` completion error, consistent with the other start-stage failures, so the opener does not wait for a timeout. - Changeset added (`minor`). ## Security consideration `/oauth-popup/start` is a GET endpoint, so `originCheckMiddleware` does not apply, unlike the POST `/sign-in/social`. This means a link to the start endpoint can now influence provider-specific authorization parameters (e.g. `login_hint`, `prompt`, `hd`). The impact looks limited: the completion message is only posted to a trusted `popupOrigin`, and a start link could already be used to begin a flow without params. I followed the approach proposed in the issue (plain pass-through with the shared schema). If maintainers prefer something stricter, such as an allowlist option on `oauthPopup()`, I'm happy to rework it. ## Testing - Server: params are forwarded to the provider authorization URL; a reserved key (`state`) is rejected; a non-string value is rejected. - Client: params are serialized into the start URL and omitted when unset. - `pnpm vitest run src/plugins/oauth-popup` passes (20 tests) and `pnpm typecheck` passes. There are no docs for `signIn.popup` under `docs/content`, so none were updated; the option is documented via JSDoc. --- ## Summary by cubic `signIn.popup` now accepts `additionalParams` so request-dependent provider parameters like `ui_locales` can be passed, matching `signIn.social` (closes #12119). - The popup client serializes `additionalParams` into the `/oauth-popup/start` URL as a JSON query param, omitted when unset. - The server validates it with `additionalAuthorizationParamsSchema` (string values only; reserved keys like `state` and `redirect_uri` rejected) and forwards the result to `createAuthorizationURL`; invalid params return an `invalid_additional_params` completion error instead of leaving the opener waiting for a timeout. ISO-8601 values stay strings rather than being coerced to dates. **Security consideration** - `/oauth-popup/start` is a GET endpoint, so `originCheckMiddleware` does not apply; a start link can now influence provider params like `login_hint` or `prompt`, but the completion message is still only posted to a trusted `popupOrigin`. **Testing** - Server tests cover forwarding, reserved-key rejection, non-string rejection, and ISO-8601 string preservation; client tests cover serialization and omission when unset. Written for commit 232cfe6b6838cbfbe9aadb79d09a17e154dbda83. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: fix(client): truncate sub-millisecond ISO date fractions to milliseconds

labels.name: core
labels.description: Core infra, API routes, session, cookies, client SDK

items.body: ## Why `parseISODate` (the reviver behind the client's global `jsonParser`, `parseDates` defaults to `true`) silently returns `Date` values that are **minutes wrong** for any ISO timestamp with sub-millisecond precision. The regex accepts 1–7 fractional-second digits: ```ts /…T(\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})(?:\.(\d{1,7}))?(?:Z|…)$/ ``` but the millisecond value is built with `parseInt(ms.padEnd(3, "0"), 10)`. `padEnd` only pads short strings — it never truncates — so a 4–7 digit fraction is read as that many *milliseconds*: ``` "2024-01-01T00:00:00.123456Z" -> 00:02:03.456 (+123 s) // should be .123 "2024-01-01T00:00:00.1234567Z" -> 00:20:34.567 (+20 min) // should be .123 ``` This violates both the function's own internal contract (its regex explicitly admits up to 7 digits) and established runtime semantics — native `new Date(iso)` truncates fractional seconds beyond milliseconds. Native JS `toISOString()` only emits 3 digits, which is why the happy path never tripped; but microsecond-precision timestamps are common from Postgres/MySQL `timestamptz` columns surfaced by adapters or `additionalFields`, and from non-JS backends. Since the reviver runs on **every** string field of **every** response, any such value comes back as a `Date` that is minutes off. ## What changed `parseISODate` now truncates the fractional part to its first three digits before padding, so 4–7 digit fractions map to the correct millisecond value (`.123456` → `.123`), matching native `Date`. 1–3 digit fractions are unchanged. ## Surface area - [ ] **Frontend UI** - [ ] **Backend API** - [ ] **Agents / LangGraph** - [ ] **Sandbox** - [ ] **Skills** - [ ] **Dependencies** - [ ] **Default behavior change** — dates with >3 fractional digits now parse correctly instead of being minutes off (a bug fix, not a new opt-in) - [ ] **Docs / tests / CI only** ## Bug fix verification - Test path that reproduces the bug: `packages/better-auth/src/client/parser.test.ts` → `parseJSON ISO date parsing > truncates … fractional seconds to milliseconds` - Did it go red on `main` and green on this branch? **yes** — on `main` the `microsecond (6 digits)` and `7 digits` cases fail (`expected 1704068434567 to be 1704067200123`); with the fix all 5 cases pass. Full file: 22 passed. ## Validation ``` cd packages/better-auth pnpm exec vitest run src/client/parser.test.ts # 22 passed pnpm exec biome check src/client/parser.ts src/client/parser.test.ts # clean ``` `pnpm typecheck` surfaces only pre-existing errors in unrelated files (`utils/url.ts`, `utils/password.ts`, `types/types.test.ts`, plus `TS6305` from an unbuilt `packages/core` in a partial local build) — identical with this branch stashed; the changed files add no new type errors. ## AI assistance **Tool(s) used:** Claude Code **How you used it:** Claude Code located the mismatch between the regex and the `padEnd` millisecond math; I independently reproduced it with a standalone Node script against the exact regex, confirmed the fix reproduces native `Date` truncation for 1–7 digit fractions, and verified the red→green test on the real vitest suite. - [x] I've read and understand every line of this change and take responsibility for it — it's not unreviewed AI output. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes ISO timestamp parsing in the client by truncating sub-millisecond fractions to milliseconds. Prevents minutes-off `Date` values when responses include 4–7 fractional digits. - **Bug Fixes** - In `parseISODate`, truncate fractional seconds with `ms.slice(0, 3).padEnd(3, "0")` to match native `Date` behavior. - Added regression tests covering 1–7 digit fractions. - Applies via the client’s global `jsonParser` used by `parseJSON` when `parseDates: true`. Written for commit 08f84573689353d91cce93123af3585d834ba689. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: fix(client): compare dates by instant in the session equality gate

labels.name: core
labels.description: Core infra, API routes, session, cookies, client SDK

items.body: ## Summary `isJsonEqual` had no `Date` branch, so two equal dates fell through to `false`. The client parser revives ISO strings into `Date` instances, so the session payload compared by the equality gate always holds dates. Two identical session responses therefore compared as different, `withEquality` never called `abort()`, and every session refetch re-rendered `useSession` consumers. Closes #10950 ## Why it happens A `Date` is not an array, and `isPlainObject` rejects it because its prototype is `Date.prototype`, so it reached the final `return false`. The gate is wired up in two places, both of which pass parsed payloads: - `client/session-atom.ts`: `isSessionAtomEqual` calls `isJsonEqual(a.data, b.data)`, then `withEquality(session, isSessionAtomEqual)` - `client/query.ts`: `withEquality(value, isAuthQueryStateEqual)` Measured on a real instance before the fix: ``` expiresAt instanceof Date: true two identical getSession() fetches, isJsonEqual -> false ``` and after: ``` two identical getSession() fetches, isJsonEqual -> true ``` ## The fix ```diff if (a === b) return true; + if (a instanceof Date || b instanceof Date) { + return ( + a instanceof Date && + b instanceof Date && + Object.is(a.getTime(), b.getTime()) + ); + } + if (Array.isArray(a) && Array.isArray(b)) { ``` Checking `a instanceof Date || b instanceof Date` first means a date is never mistaken for a plain object, and a date compared against a non-date is correctly unequal. `Object.is` is used so two invalid dates (`NaN`) stay equal rather than reporting a change on every set, which would reintroduce the same loop for malformed values. The JSDoc now records that dates are compared by instant, and why. ## Tests Four tests added to the existing `isJsonEqual` suite: equal instants, different instants, session-shaped data holding dates, and a date compared against a non-date. The two positive tests fail on the unpatched code with `expected false to be true`, which is the bug. Full `equality.test.ts` is 21/21 and the whole `client/` suite is 119/119. `pnpm typecheck` reports no new errors. The 8 pre-existing `schemaName` errors in `packages/cli/test/generate.test.ts` are present on a clean `main` as well and are unrelated. ## Risk Behaviour only becomes more permissive: payloads that were previously reported as changed on every fetch can now be recognised as unchanged. No API or type change. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the client equality gate so identical session payloads containing dates no longer re-render. Previously `isJsonEqual` returned false for `Date` values, so the gate never aborted updates and every session refetch re-rendered consumers. **Bug Fixes** - Detect dates via the `[object Date]` brand and extract the instant with `Date.prototype.getTime.call`, so dates from other realms compare correctly. - Compare `getTime()` with `Object.is` so two invalid dates are equal and avoid update thrash. - Add tests for cross-realm dates, spoofed `Date` tags, equal/different instants, session-shaped payloads, nested dates in arrays, and date vs non-date. - No API or type changes. Written for commit 9c723476194cd3d356b43e7825285a0ba88e82b5. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: fix(oauth-provider): skip POST rewrite when OAuth query unsigned

labels.name: identity
labels.description: OAuth/OIDC provider, device flow

items.body: ## Summary `oauthProviderClient()`'s `oauth-provider-signin` `onRequest` hook was re-serializing every non-GET/DELETE body whenever `window.location.search` was non-empty — even when there was no signed OAuth query (`sig` + `ba_param`). Parsing with `safeJSONParse` revived ISO-8601 strings into `Date`s, so `JSON.stringify` corrupted date-like fields (added/truncated ms), turned form-urlencoded bodies into JSON objects, and could turn array bodies into objects. Reset-password pages with `?token=` were a real-world footgun. **Fix:** - Return early before any body parse/re-serialize when `buildSignedOAuthQuery(window.location.search)` is empty. - On the signed-query merge path, parse JSON bodies with plain `JSON.parse` instead of `safeJSONParse` so other fields are not date-revived. Fixes #12072 ## Test plan - [x] Added `packages/oauth-provider/src/client.test.ts` covering: - unsigned query leaves JSON (incl. ISO dates), form-urlencoded, and array bodies untouched - empty / missing search leaves bodies untouched - GET/DELETE skip rewrite even with a signed query - signed query merges `oauth_query` while preserving ISO date strings - existing `oauth_query` is left alone - [x] Local: `pnpm exec vitest run packages/oauth-provider/src/client.test.ts packages/oauth-provider/src/signed-query.test.ts` → 15 passed - [ ] CI green on this PR --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the OAuth provider sign-in hook rewriting POST/PUT/PATCH bodies whenever the page had a query string, even when it wasn't a signed OAuth query. Unsigned query strings like `?token=` used to re-serialize bodies via `safeJSONParse`, which corrupted ISO-8601 date strings (added/truncated milliseconds), turned form-urlencoded bodies into JSON objects, and could turn arrays into objects. The hook now returns early when the window has no search or `buildSignedOAuthQuery` finds no signed query, and uses plain `JSON.parse` when merging the signed query so date fields stay intact. Fixes #12072. - Added `packages/oauth-provider/src/client.test.ts` covering unsigned, empty, and signed query scenarios, plus GET/DELETE skip behavior. Written for commit 50eaa3433e9e1e619b8f61c9ba6d25c4c17b6c8c. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: fix(db): recover null-user session cache entries

labels.name: database
labels.description: Database layer, all adapters, schema, migrations

items.body:
Closes #10884.

Secondary-only sessions now survive a transient user lookup miss during creation. The cache keeps the session payload without serializing `user: null`; later `findSession` and `findSessions` calls treat a missing or legacy null user as a cache miss and read the authoritative user row.

Recovered reads deliberately do not heal or write back incomplete cache entries, whether `user` is omitted or is legacy `null`. This avoids a read-then-write race that could recreate a session token after `deleteSession` or `deleteSessions` revoked it.

Complete cache entries keep the existing zero-query fast path.

Tests cover the initial transient miss, recovery of missing and legacy null-user entries through single and multi-session reads, both session-revocation races, secondary-storage write failures, authoritative lookup failures, and the valid cache-hit control.

Verified with:

- `pnpm vitest packages/better-auth/src/db/internal-adapter.test.ts packages/better-auth/src/db/secondary-storage.test.ts --run` (86 passed)
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm exec biome check packages/better-auth/src/db/internal-adapter.ts packages/better-auth/src/db/internal-adapter.test.ts`
- `pnpm changeset status`
- `git diff --check`

Codex assisted with reproducing the cache failure, developing the regression coverage, and reviewing the implementation. I reviewed the session-storage contract, the final diff, and all results above.

items.body: Magic Link now redeems only records issued for Magic Link. Its verification identifiers and database-backed OAuth/SAML state use separate prefixes, and Magic Link validates the stored record purpose and shape before consumption and again on the atomically consumed result before issuing a session. Known mismatched records are rejected without consuming them. OAuth state cookies and each OAuth Proxy payload use separate derived encryption keys while retaining versioned secret rotation within each purpose. There is no database schema change, user/account migration, or change to endpoint signatures and option types. Previously issued Magic Links and sign-in or account-linking flows using Better Auth-generated OAuth/SAML state must be restarted after the cutover. Upgrade servers sharing verification storage, nodes serving the same cookie-backed state flow, and all OAuth Proxy participants together. Update custom `verification.storeIdentifier.overrides` rules or integrations that inspect these identifiers to use `magic-link:` and `auth-state:`. Pre-upgrade encrypted OAuth/SAML state cookies and OAuth Proxy payloads are rejected without a compatibility fallback. The documentation and patch changesets explain the cutover, unchanged token/callback values, custom hashing behavior, and the trust required when production handles OAuth Proxy callbacks for development or preview deployments. --- ## Summary by cubic Magic Link now redeems only records issued for Magic Link. Its verification identifiers and database-backed OAuth/SAML state use separate prefixes (`magic-link:` and `auth-state:`), and Magic Link validates a record's purpose and shape before consuming it, rejecting mismatched records without deleting them so other flows' records stay intact. The atomically consumed record is validated again before a session is issued, and display names, including date-shaped strings, are preserved during verification. OAuth state cookies and each OAuth Proxy payload use separate derived encryption keys while retaining versioned secret rotation within each purpose. There is no database schema change, user/account migration, or change to endpoint signatures and option types. Previously issued Magic Links and sign-in or account-linking flows using Better Auth-generated OAuth/SAML state must be restarted after the cutover. Upgrade servers sharing verification storage, nodes serving the same cookie-backed state flow, and all OAuth Proxy participants together. Update custom `verification.storeIdentifier.overrides` rules or integrations that inspect these identifiers to use `magic-link:` and `auth-state:`. Pre-upgrade encrypted OAuth/SAML state cookies and OAuth Proxy payloads are rejected without a compatibility fallback. The documentation and patch changesets explain the cutover, unchanged token/callback values, custom hashing behavior, and the trust required when production handles OAuth Proxy callbacks. items.title: fix(client): deduplicate settled session requests during Suspense retries

labels.name: core
labels.description: Core infra, API routes, session, cookies, client SDK

labels.name: locked
labels.description: Locked conversations after being closed for 7 days

items.body: Prevent transient Suspense remounts from reissuing a settled session request. ### Before Request deduplication ended as soon as the request settled, allowing a transient remount to immediately issue another request. ### Policy | Condition | Behavior | | --- | --- | | Request in flight | Reuse the request | | Fresh result | Skip remount revalidation during the dedupe interval | | Stale, failed, or aborted result | Revalidate on the next mount | | Explicit refetch, session change, or expiration | Revalidate | --- ## Summary by cubic Deduplicates settled session requests during React Suspense retries to prevent duplicate fetches on transient remounts. Previously dedupe ended on settle; now successful results are reused until the smaller of `nanostores` `STORE_UNMOUNT_DELAY` or session expiry, while failed/aborted or incomplete refreshes always retry. **Details** - Request policy: reuse in-flight; treat successful results as fresh during the dedupe window; revalidate on explicit refetch, session signal change, or expiry; never mark failed refreshes as fresh. - Implementation: separate session “flight” from mount freshness with a revisioned flight; set `freshUntil` only for a “fresh” outcome on the current revision; align dedupe with `STORE_UNMOUNT_DELAY`. - Tests: add coverage for Suspense retry dedupe, remount after failure, retry after incomplete refresh, and revalidation when the session signal flips. Written for commit 98b94d2113d6abb0b74213aa42459412bd2eacaa. Summary will update on new commits.

items.body: Brings the stable fixes released on `main` as v1.6.14 through v1.6.16 into `next`, replacing the bot's auto-sync #9856 which could not merge. The conflicts were almost entirely next's breaking OAuth refactors (the shared id_token verifier, `grantedScopes`, RFC 8707 resource indicators, back-channel logout, `max_age`, and the electron S256 rewrite) overlapping main's patch fixes, most of them from "fix: address bug findings across packages" (#9974). A few resolutions are worth a closer look. PayPal keeps next's deliberate removal of id_token sign-in, so main's re-added verification is dropped. Google's hosted-domain enforcement was ported onto next's shared id_token verifier, which previously had no `hd` concept; it now applies on the id_token sign-in path, not just the callback. The SSO provider-name trust-laundering fix was threaded through next's refactored sign-in seam (`resolve-account` and the SAML pipeline). Per-client grant-type enforcement is reconciled with next's resource-binding argument so the `unauthorized_client` rejection still fires. Several test files that auto-merged from main referenced helpers that next had renamed, made async, or removed; those were adapted to next's current APIs without weakening coverage. The catalog bump to `better-call` 1.3.6 carries over with a regenerated lockfile. Closes #9856 --- ## Summary by cubic Syncs `next` with fixes from `main` v1.6.14–v1.6.16 and reconciles OAuth/session changes. This brings stronger security, safer session/cookie handling, and some DX/docs updates. - **Bug Fixes** - CSRF: validate `Origin`/`Referer` even without cookies; respect Fetch Metadata; block untrusted `redirectTo`. - Cookies/session: prefer `__Secure-` cookies, ignore empty secure values, and clear mismatched account cookies; require a fresh session to list sessions; honor server-side session deletion in session update/token routes; make cookie-cache/refresh flags strictly OR’d; resolve sessions from the authoritative store when creating API keys. - OAuth/SSO: enforce Google Workspace `hd` on id_token; verify Facebook access tokens with `debug_token` against configured apps; require a stable subject id in generic OAuth; prevent SSO “provider id” trust-laundering with `trustProviderByName`; avoid refreshing with another user’s account cookie; consume SAML AuthnRequest atomically; allow POST on `userinfo`. - SIWE: parse ERC‑4361 messages and bind them to the server nonce/domain/chain; reject mismatches. - Organization: harden invitations (opaque ids, ownership/verification gates), scope team ids and team lists to the invited org, and mark plugin-owned session fields as non-input. - Admin: gate role/email changes behind proper permissions, return 404 for missing users, and disallow password changes via update-user; add error codes. - API keys: avoid writeback of stale verification state; verification uses partial updates to prevent clobbering; tests added. - Core/JWT: isolate JWKS cache per issuer to avoid `kid` collisions. - Passkeys: resolve authenticator names from `aaguid` at read time. - Schema: optional fields accept `null` (e.g. org `logo`). - Hooks: run configured `before`/`after` hooks once per HTTP dispatch; internal endpoint calls (e.g. `getSession`) don’t re-run them. - **Migration** - Admin: if your app updates user emails via the admin API, grant the new `user:set-email` permission. - Sessions: `listUserSessions` now requires a fresh session. Adjust `session.freshAge` or re-prompt users as needed. - SIWE: clients must send a valid ERC‑4361 message; the plugin now validates nonce, domain, address, chain id, and time bounds. - Two-Factor: during a 2FA challenge `newSession` is `null`; null-check it in server-side hooks. Written for commit d7bba8ee33f15fa2526022d1bc91e0e431440c12. Summary will update on new commits.
